newsitem.title: RUSSIA: SOCCER-UNFANCIED ROTOR STAY TOP IN RUSSIAN TITLE RACE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-UNFANCIED ROTOR STAY TOP IN RUSSIAN TITLE RACE.

text.p: Top scorer Oleg Veretennikov's 40th-minute strike was enough to preserve Rotor Volgograd's one-point lead in the Russian premier league on Saturday, with just three games to play.

But Moscow powerhouses Spartak and CSKA both won -- CSKA at the expense of champions Alania Vladikavkaz -- to keep up the pressure on unfancied provincial Rotor, who overcame mid-table Baltika Kaliningrad 1-0 at home.

Spartak Moscow moved up to second, international midfielder Ilya Tsymbalar's spectacular 87th-minute solo strike rounding off a powerful attacking display that sank Moscow rivals Dynamo 3-1 and served notice the 1994 champions should not be written off.

Vladikavkaz, their end of season blighted by a dismal showing in Europe that included a 7-2 drubbing at home to Glasgow Rangers, went down 2-0 in the capital to CSKA, allowing CSKA to draw level on points and push Alania down to fourth.

As all too often this season, the Caucasus team's defenders were absent when Samaroni found himself in possession in the box after 40 minutes. Movsesyan turned two defenders to make it 2-0 just after the hour. Dzhioyev's sending off in the 66th minute, ended a bad day for Vladikavkaz.
Across town, Spartak, who travel to Germany to face Hamburg in the UEFA Cup on Wednesday, dominated Dynamo for much of the game but again looked fragile on the break.

Coach Georgy Yartsev criticised keeper Ruslan Nigmatullin for Dmitry Cheryshev's last-minute consolation goal for Dynamo and said the intense competition between Nigmatullin and Alexander Filimonov for the number one jersey was far from over.
Up front, however, Spartak had plenty of good ideas, orchestrated by captain Tysmbalar, showing no sign of his recent injury trouble as he tormented the Dynamo defence.
Vadim Yevseyev put Spartak in front in 57 minutes, Vladimir Dzhubanov laying back neatly for the left back to thunder the ball past Dynamo keeper Andrei Smetanin.

With the Dynamo defence still claiming an earlier foul on Sergei Nerkasov, Dmitry Alenichev made it 2-0 in 76 minutes. Then Tsymbalar wrapped it up, weaving his way past two defenders to send a perfectly weighted 20-metre lob over Smetanin.
Dynamo, who started the day just a point behind Spartak, are still in with a chance, coach Adamas Golodets insisted. They remain in fifth, five points behind Rotor.

Yartsev said Spartak faced a tough run-in to the November 3 league finale, away at Hamburg in the UEFA cup on Wednesday and at Torpedo Moscow in the league next Saturday. Rotor, who put Manchester United out of the UEFA Cup last year, have not played in Europe this season.
"There's a big load on our lads," Yartsev said. "Obviously Rotor have the advantage and they're a pretty good side."
